cards.explanation: The answer is any children. Abram says, "…since I remain childless, and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?" (Genesis 15:2). He's holding the biggest empty spot in his tent up to God. I think that's a hard thing to say out loud, and he says it anyway.

The word is servant. Abram says, "…a servant in my household will be my heir." (Genesis 15:3). I think he's laying out his problem for God. Then God answers, "This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir." (Genesis 15:4).

The answer is False. God tells Abram, "This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir." (Genesis 15:4). Abram names Eliezer, and God says no, not him. God gives a clear answer to Abram's worry.

The blanks are stars and offspring. God says, "Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able." (Genesis 15:5). He takes Abram outside to do it, and I bet most of us would quit counting around star number twelve. My sprinkle jar is easy to count next to that sky. Then God says, "So shall your offspring be." (Genesis 15:5). Abram has no child at this point, and God points him to the stars. I think that's a lot to take in.

The answer is that he believes the LORD. "Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness." (Genesis 15:6). Nothing about his tent had changed yet. He still had no child, and he believed anyway.

The answer is to give him this land. God says He brought Abram out of Ur "…to give you this land to possess." (Genesis 15:7). Ur of the Chaldeans was where the trip started. God tells him where it was headed.

The answer is how he can know he will possess it. Abram asks, "Lord GOD, how can I know that I will possess it?" (Genesis 15:8). It's an honest question, asked right to God. I think it's the kind of thing a person says out loud when they want to be sure.

The answer is True. God asked for "…a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon." (Genesis 15:9). Then "…Abram brought all these to Him…" (Genesis 15:10). He brings the whole list, no shortcuts.

The answer is False. "And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away." (Genesis 15:11). So Abram doesn't hand them over. He steps in and shoos them off. I picture him waving his arms like I wave my mustache at a crumb thief.

The answer is True. God says, "But I will judge the nation they serve as slaves…" (Genesis 15:14). He speaks about the very place where Abram's descendants will be enslaved. God doesn't leave that hardship unanswered.

The answer is that they will depart with many possessions. God says, "…afterward they will depart with many possessions." (Genesis 15:14). They don't just get out. They walk out carrying a lot with them.

The word is peace. God tells Abram, "You, however, will go to your fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age." (Genesis 15:15). After hearing about hard years ahead for his descendants, Abram gets this word for himself. I think that's a comfort.

The answer is that their sin is not yet complete. God says, "…for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete." (Genesis 15:16). Iniquity means sin. That's the reason He gives for why the return isn't sooner.

The answer is False. "…a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appeared and passed between the halves of the carcasses." (Genesis 15:17). They go down the middle, through the path between the halves. Abram laid those halves opposite each other, so that's the way through.

The answer is that the LORD makes a covenant with Abram. "On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram…" (Genesis 15:18). Abram had asked, "…how can I know that I will possess it?" (Genesis 15:8). This is what happens that day. A covenant is a solemn promise, and this one is God's.
